verdict.text: Immediate for development workspace installs; up to 10 business days preliminary and 10 weeks functional review for public Slack Marketplace listing.
verdict.label: Inferred
verdict.note: Developers can create an app and install it to their development workspace immediately without review. Public listing in the Slack Marketplace requires passing an automated and manual multi-stage review.

hands_on_time.label: Inferred
hands_on_time.note: Registering an app, obtaining credentials, setting up redirect URIs, and configuring scopes takes roughly 15 to 30 minutes.

waiting_time.label: Inferred
waiting_time.note: Workspace-level installs are instant. For Marketplace listing, preliminary review takes up to 10 business days and functional review takes up to 10 weeks.

prerequisites.text: A Slack account and access to a development workspace where the app will be built and tested.
prerequisites.label: Inferred
prerequisites.note: Slack requires signing into a workspace to access app management and to install an undistributed app.

prerequisites.text: For Marketplace review submission, your app must be installed on 10 or more active workspaces used in the past 28 days.
prerequisites.label: Sourced
prerequisites.quote: Your app has been installed on 10 or more active workspaces and the service has been tested on those workspaces

setup_steps.text: Go to the Slack App Management console at https://api.slack.com/apps and sign in with your Slack account.
setup_steps.label: Sourced
setup_steps.quote: Include both your app's client ID, which is found in the App Management page, and a comma-separated list of scopes

setup_steps.text: Create a new app by choosing either 'From scratch' or using an App Manifest, give it an app name, and pick your development workspace.
setup_steps.label: Inferred
setup_steps.note: Standard app creation flow in Slack App Management.

setup_steps.text: In the left sidebar under 'OAuth & Permissions', configure your HTTPS Redirect URL (must not include an anchor '#').
setup_steps.label: Sourced
setup_steps.quote: Alternatively, you can configure a Redirect URL in the App Management page under OAuth & Permissions. A Redirect URL must also use HTTPS.

setup_steps.text: Under 'OAuth & Permissions', add the required Bot Token Scopes and User Token Scopes needed for your integration.
setup_steps.label: Sourced
setup_steps.quote: Bot scopes should be added as scope=<bot_scope>, and user scopes should be added as user_scope=<user_scope>.

setup_steps.text: Retrieve your Client ID and Client Secret from the App Management page for exchanging authorization codes via oauth.v2.access.
setup_steps.label: Sourced

setup_steps.text: Redirect users to https://slack.com/oauth/v2/authorize with your client_id, scopes, and redirect_uri to initiate installation.
setup_steps.label: Sourced
setup_steps.quote: To request scopes, redirect Slack users to https://slack.com/oauth/v2/authorize.

setup_steps.text: If publishing publicly, test across 10 active workspaces and navigate to 'Submit to the Slack Marketplace' in your app configuration page.
setup_steps.label: Sourced
setup_steps.quote: Your app submission (and subsequent updates to your app) happens from the Submit to the Slack Marketplace section of your app's configuration page.

scopes.text: chat:write: Send messages as your Slack app.
scopes.label: Sourced
scopes.quote: Send messages as your Slack app

scopes.text: channels:read: View basic information about public channels in a workspace.
scopes.label: Sourced
scopes.quote: View basic information about public channels in a workspace

scopes.text: channels:history: View messages and other content in public channels that your Slack app has been added to.
scopes.label: Sourced
scopes.quote: View messages and other content in public channels that your Slack app has been added to

scopes.text: commands: Add shortcuts and slash commands that people can use.
scopes.label: Sourced
scopes.quote: Add shortcuts and slash commands that people can use

scopes.text: incoming-webhook: Post messages to specific channels in Slack.
scopes.label: Sourced
scopes.quote: Post messages to specific channels in Slack

scopes.text: users:read: View people in a workspace.
scopes.label: Sourced

limits_before_approval.text: Undistributed apps can only be installed on the workspace where they were created, unless configured for an Enterprise org that supports org-wide installs.
limits_before_approval.label: Sourced
limits_before_approval.quote: Your app can only be installed on the workspace that owns it. Slack asks the user to sign in to that workspace

limits_before_approval.text: Apps must reach at least 10 active workspaces before they are eligible to submit for public Slack Marketplace review.
limits_before_approval.label: Sourced
limits_before_approval.quote: Your app has been installed on 10 or more active workspaces and the service has been tested on those workspaces

limits_before_approval.text: Web API calls are rate limited per method per workspace per app across four tiers (Tier 1: 1+/min, Tier 2: 20+/min, Tier 3: 50+/min, Tier 4: 100+/min).
limits_before_approval.label: Sourced
limits_before_approval.quote: Broadly, you'll encounter limits like these, applied on a " per API method per workspace/team per app" basis.

limits_before_approval.text: Message posting is limited to 1 message per second per channel, with short bursts allowed.
limits_before_approval.label: Sourced
limits_before_approval.quote: In general, apps may post no more than one message per second per channel, whether a message is posted via chat.postMessage

limits_before_approval.text: Events API deliveries max out at 30,000 per workspace per app per 60 minutes.
limits_before_approval.label: Sourced
limits_before_approval.quote: Event deliveries to your server via the Events API currently max out at 30,000 per workspace/team per app per 60 minutes.

approval_process.text: Automated tests run during the submission process and detected issues must be resolved before manual submission.
approval_process.label: Sourced
approval_process.quote: Before you can submit your app, we will run some automated tests on your app. Once you’ve fixed any issues we detect, you can submit

approval_process.text: Preliminary review takes up to 10 business days, reviewing listing details, links, documentation, and scope justifications.
approval_process.label: Sourced
approval_process.quote: Currently, the preliminary part of the review takes up to 10 business days to receive feedback, while the functional review takes up to 10

approval_process.text: Functional review takes up to 10 weeks for new submissions and tests the end-to-end user experience, install/uninstall, and scope usage.
approval_process.label: Sourced
approval_process.quote: Once your app enters this stage of the review, your submission will be assigned to a reviewer and you’ll receive feedback about your app’s

approval_process.text: Endpoints are checked for TLS and request signing verification, though Slack does not perform code reviews.
approval_process.label: Sourced
approval_process.quote: Tests an app’s endpoints for TLS and request signing verification (used by apps to validate requests they receive are coming from Slack).

approval_process.text: Once approved and published to the Slack Marketplace, the live app configuration is locked and changes require resubmitting for review.
approval_process.label: Sourced
approval_process.quote: Once your app is published in the Slack Marketplace, the live version of your app is locked.

likely_blockers.text: Not meeting the minimum requirement of 10 active workspace installations blocks submission to the Marketplace.
likely_blockers.label: Sourced
likely_blockers.quote: apps that do not meet this requirement will be blocked from submitting to the Marketplace

likely_blockers.text: Requesting legacy, coded workflow, or high-privilege scopes such as admin.*, search:read, triggers:*, read, post, or client.
likely_blockers.label: Sourced
likely_blockers.quote: you’ll also need to ensure that your app does not request legacy/restricted scopes, scopes that provide extensive access to workspace data, or coded workflow scopes

likely_blockers.text: Requesting scopes for future functionality rather than features actively available and testable in the current app build.
likely_blockers.label: Sourced
likely_blockers.quote: Please do not submit your app with scopes for a feature that you plan to build at some point in future.

likely_blockers.text: Failing to provide test account credentials (or sufficiently long free trials) for third-party or paid services required by the app.
likely_blockers.label: Sourced
likely_blockers.quote: If a paid account is required for your service, you’ll need to share login credentials with us for an account with the required level

likely_blockers.text: Frequent bugs, low quality, or submitting in private beta before full end-to-end and uninstall testing is completed.
likely_blockers.label: Sourced
likely_blockers.quote: If your app is submitted with bugs, poor user experience, or we repeatedly run into issues of low quality when reviewing, we will return it

agent_can_do: Explain bot vs user scopes and provide appropriate scope lists for your integration.
Generate OAuth authorize URLs with parameters like client_id, scopes, and redirect_uri.
Format API requests for token exchange using oauth.v2.access.
Draft app manifest YAML or JSON configurations for app setup.
you_must_do: Log in to the Slack App Management console at https://api.slack.com/apps.
Create the app and copy your Client ID and Client Secret.
Configure your HTTPS Redirect URL and authorize test workspace installs.
Fulfill the 10-active-workspace requirement and submit for Slack Marketplace review if distributing publicly.

open_questions.text: Can an app be distributed to multiple external workspaces via direct install links without submitting to the Slack Marketplace, beyond initial test workspaces?
open_questions.label: Uncertain
open_questions.note: Documentation discusses workspace installs on 10 active workspaces prior to Marketplace submission, but does not state the hard cap on direct link installs without Marketplace listing.
